documents.title: Comprehensive Artificial Intelligence Use Policy (SUS-1-004)
documents.stance_why: The policy hands coursework decisions to instructors: "AI policies fall under faculty discretion" and "faculty have the right to regulate and/or prohibit student use of AI, as they see fit". It sets no single default for all courses and names no tiers, so it delegates, although it also lists permitted uses "at faculty discretion" and says use "without instructor permission" violates the honor code.
documents.summary: System-wide policy (SUS-1-004) that sets a framework, definitions, privacy and attribution duties, and an Advisory Council and appeal process. It permits reference, ideation, translation and tutoring uses in coursework at faculty discretion with citation, and leaves each instructor to regulate or prohibit AI in their courses. By default, uncited or unpermitted student AI use violates the honor code.

notes: Reconciled from coders A and B. Two included university-layer documents. The policy brief labels the policy SUS-6-001 (approved May 1, 2025) while the Drive full text is SUS-1-004 (effective 07/18/2025, board-signed Sept 2025); they may be the same policy or campus versus system versions. The PDF text has spacing artifacts (e.g. 'discl ose'); anchors copy them exactly. Full text comes from a third-party Drive link. Technical glossary definitions (Narrow, Reactive, Limited Memory, Theory of Mind, AGI, Deep Learning, Data Science, Machine Learning, NLP) found only by A were dropped as not policy statements; definitions of AI, AI System, Generative AI, Agentic AI, LLM, PII and Academic Integrity were kept as P61. A's duplicate/rationale units dropped: 'promotes trust, fairness, and accountability', 'promoting innovation and learning', and the repeated 'is permitted, at faculty discretion'. A's translation unit was recoded UNCOVERED (permitted translation use). Original coder notes: A: Glossary definitions were each coded as P61 units; B: policy numbers and dates differ between brief and full text.
